content_preview.title: Kubernetes v1.38 Sneak Peek Lists cgroup Driver, kubectl WebSocket and Pod-Level Resource Changes
content_preview.summary: The Kubernetes project previewed v1.38, due December 16, detailing a breaking cgroup-driver change, removed kubectl WebSocket env vars, and three features graduating to stable.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Kubernetes release team published a sneak peek of version 1.38, titled "Kubernetes v1.38 Sneak Peek," on the project's [official blog](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2026/11/23/kubernetes-v1-38-sneak-peek/) on November 23, listing deprecations, removals, and breaking changes ahead of the release, which the post says "is planned for Wednesday, December 16th, 2026." The post, credited to release-team members Aaron Braundmeier, Arsh Sharma, Kirti Goyal, Omar Nasser, Sayan Chowdhury and...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece: an Overview establishing the sneak-peek's provenance and caveats, a dedicated section for the single breaking change (CRI cgroup-driver detection), a section for removals/deprecations, a section for stable-graduating features plus the new alpha EvictionRequest API, and a closing 'What We Don't Know' section that correctly frames the piece as preliminary. Word count 862, within the News 400-1200 range.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 6 source snapshots from disk after verifying each sha256 matched the manifest (decompressed hash recomputed and compared byte-for-byte against manifest.json; all 6 matched exactly). source-0.html.gz (kubernetes.io blog, 'Kubernetes v1.38 Sneak Peek', published Nov 23 2026) supports the Overview, the cgroup-driver breaking change, the kubectl WebSocket removal, the kuberc name-field removal, the cgroup v1 phase-out note, the admission-webhook virtual-resource change, the pod-level-resources swap-behavior note, the DRA partitionable-devices description, the EvictionRequest API description, and the December 16 2026 release date -- confirmed present verbatim in the raw page text, author byline (Aaron Braundmeier, Arsh Sharma, Kirti Goyal, Omar Nasser, Sayan Chowdhury, Urvashi Choubey) matches exactly. source-1.html.gz (KEP-4033 kep.yaml) confirms stage: stable, milestone.stable: v1.34, feature-gates[0].name: KubeletCgroupDriverFromCRI -- matches the article's claim that KEP-4033 'reached general availability in v1.34' under that gate. source-2.html.gz (KEP-2837) confirms stage: stable, milestone.stable: v1.38, feature-gates[0].name: PodLevelResources -- matches the article's claim. source-3.html.gz (KEP-4815) confirms stage: stable, milestone.stable: v1.38, feature-gates[0].name: DRAPartitionableDevices -- matches. source-4.html.gz (KEP-4563) confirms stage: alpha, milestone.alpha: v1.38, feature-gates[0].name: EvictionRequestAPI -- matches the article's claim that this KEP lists v1.38 as its alpha milestone. source-5.html.gz (KEP-3104) confirms stage: stable, milestone.stable: '1.38', feature-gates[0].name: KUBECTL_KUBERC -- matches. No suspicious_patterns flagged in the manifest for any of the 6 sources; none found on manual reading either. Anthropic disclosure: not required - the article does not mention Anthropic, Claude, or any Anthropic-operated product as subject, in the headline/summary/lead, or anywhere in the body.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Independently extracted and quote-by-quote checked all 24 double-quoted spans in body_markdown against the raw decompressed kubernetes.io blog text (did not rely on the writer's or the automated script's own quote matching). 23 of 24 are exact verbatim matches to contiguous source text (code-formatting of identifiers like `cgroupDriver`, `systemd`, `RuntimeConfig` is the only rendering difference, and several quotes legitimately drop a parenthetical aside from the source while quoting the text on either side of it, which is acceptable paraphrase practice since the dropped material is not inside the quotation marks). One issue found: in the Overview paragraph the article quotes '"is not a commitment."' with a terminal period, but in the source this exact wordstring is not a complete sentence -- the actual source sentence is 'This is not a commitment and the release content is subject to change.' The article's own 'What We Don't Know' section later quotes this same source sentence correctly and in full ('"is not a commitment and the release content is subject to change."'). So the article contains both the correct full quotation and, earlier, a truncated version of the same clause dressed with a period it doesn't have in the source, implying a sentence break that isn't there. This does not misstate any fact -- the clipped words are still accurate on their own terms, and the fuller, correct version appears later in the same piece -- but it is not a verbatim quotation as presented, so it is flagged as a clarification-severity correction rather than waved through silently. All five KEP-derived specifics (feature gate names, milestone versions, stage designations) were verified directly against the raw kep.yaml fields as rendered in the GitHub blob pages (see source_verification) and are accurate without exception.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and technical throughout. No editorializing, no unsupported characterizations. Breaking change vs. stable-graduation vs. new-alpha are each labeled correctly and consistently with the blog post's own framing (confirmed against the blog's own section headers: 'Breaking changes in Kubernetes v1.38', 'Featured enhancements of Kubernetes v1.38' listing kuberc/pod-level-resources/DRA-partitionable-devices as expected to graduate to stable, and 'EvictionRequest API (alpha)' explicitly labeled alpha).
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate. Searched src/content/articles/ for prior Kubernetes coverage: '03-kubernetes-137-sets-timelines-to-retire-ipvs-mode...' (2026-11-03) covers IPVS/kube-dns retirement timelines for 1.37, a different release and different topics. '07-nodejs-aspnet-core-23-cpythons-jit-and-kubernetes-kube-dns...' (2026-11-07) is a cross-project notice-period comparison centered on kube-dns, not this story. '07-kubernetes-project-reminds-operators...cgroup-v1-nodes...since-v135' (2026-10-07) and '12-kubernetes-137-landing-august-26...' (2026-08-12) are the prior release's sneak-peek/cgroup-v1 coverage; this submission's one-paragraph mention of the ongoing cgroup v1 phase-out restates status quo already covered there, but it is a single subordinate paragraph, not the article's subject -- the article's five substantive topics (CRI cgroup-driver breaking change, kubectl WebSocket var removal, kuberc/pod-level-resources/DRA-partitionable-devices graduations, and the new EvictionRequest API alpha) are all previewed here for the first time in the Herald's archive. No prior 'v1.38 Sneak Peek' or 'v1.38' article exists (grep of src/content/articles/ for 'sneak peek' and 'v1.38' returned no hits for this release). Confirmed genuinely new topic, not a rewrite or recap of existing coverage.
concerns: The Overview paragraph quotes 'is not a commitment.' with a terminal period that does not exist in the source at that point -- the source sentence continues '...and the release content is subject to change.' The article itself quotes the complete, correct sentence later in 'What We Don't Know.' Filed as a clarification-severity correction (src/content/corrections/2026-11/24-kubernetes-v138-sneak-peek-lists-cgroup-driver-kubectl-websocket-and-pod-level-resource-changes.json).
editor_notes.overall_assessment: A well-sourced, accurately characterized preview piece: all five KEP milestone/feature-gate claims checked out exactly against the raw kep.yaml files, the breaking-change/graduation/alpha distinctions match the blog's own framing, and 23 of 24 quoted spans are verbatim. One truncated quotation in the Overview section is addressed with a public clarification record rather than silently waved through. The subject matter -- a sneak peek of an unreleased Kubernetes version -- is useful to a defined operator/platform-engineering audience but is inherently preliminary (the post itself says the list 'is not a commitment') and incremental in impact. Featured candidacy: 0 - a routine, properly-sourced preview of upcoming changes for a defined Kubernetes-operator audience, not a broad-impact or exceptional story.
